### 3.6 Footer : ligne en cours, ligne en erreur (Rule 128)

Précédence : error > warn > info > status. Un détail de ligne est de niveau `Status` (sans minuteur, recalculé à chaque trame), composé « détail de ligne · progression globale ». Le détail est tronqué d'abord (Rule 124 : la hauteur ne change pas).

Ligne en cours (`ws`, ligne `api` sélectionnée, sync de 12 dépôts) :

```
(blanc)
        ● Syncing ~/w/app/api · 3/12 repositories
```

Niveau `Status`, texte de couleur ordinaire. Pas de spinner de footer ici : la pastille bouge déjà sur la ligne ; un spinner doublerait le mouvement.

Ligne en erreur, en trois temps :

| Temps | Niveau | Texte | Couleur |
|---|---|---|---|
| t = 0 à 3 s (l'échec arrive) | `Error`, avec minuteur | `Failed to scan ~/w/app/web — trivy could not pull the database` | `ColorFooterError`, gras |
| t > 3 s, ligne `web` sélectionnée | `Status`, persistant | `⊗ ~/w/app/web: last scan failed — trivy could not pull the database` | `ColorFooterInfo`, normal |
| t > 3 s, autre ligne sélectionnée | `Status` | le détail de cette ligne, ou la progression globale seule | idem |

La pastille rouge fixe persiste jusqu'à la prochaine tentative sur la ligne ; seul le texte de footer passe de l'événement à l'état (décision de l'architect, Q4). Si une opération est en cours sur la même ligne, l'échec masqué est en suffixe (§1.2). Si un autre `Error` arrive pendant les 3 s, il prend le pas (précédence inchangée).

## 4. Fréquence et « en file »

**Tranché (D7) : 1 Hz (500 ms allumé, 500 ms éteint), phase déduite de l'horloge.**

| | 1 Hz (recommandé) | 2 Hz |
|---|---|---|
| WCAG 2.3.1 (≤ 3 flashs/s) | 1 flash/s : marge de 3 | 2 flashs/s : sous le seuil, marge de 1,5 |
| Perception | pouls calme, ne distrait pas pendant la lecture d'un tableau | réveille l'œil, se lit comme une alerte |
| Coût (SSH) | une réécriture de cellule par ligne par seconde | le double |
| Cadence du tick routeur | 500 ms (déjà prévue par l'architect) | 250 ms |
| Détection de l'état gelé | un blocage de plus de 1 s se voit | idem, plus vite |

Justification complémentaire : la surface qui clignote est minuscule (une cellule par ligne), la variation de luminance est modeste (anneau contre disque, même couleur), et rien ne clignote en rouge. Toutes les pastilles clignotent **en phase** : un décalage entre lignes créerait un effet de vague qui augmente le flash perçu. La phase vient du temps du message de tick (`on = (t.UnixMilli() / 500) % 2 == 0`) : survit à un changement de cadence, testable. 2 Hz resterait une constante à changer si le pilote la jugeait trop lente (le premier point de contrôle peut le rouvrir).

**« En file » : statique** (`◴`, `ColorActivityNeutral`). Voir §1.3. Passage `◴` à `●`/`○` à la prise en charge ; le tick démarre alors, une seule fois.

## 5. Cas limites

1. **Plusieurs pastilles simultanées dans une vue.** Toutes en phase, pas de plafond. Un lot de N scans donne 1 en cours + (N−1) en file : un seul clignotant (le tick est partagé) et N−1 `◴` fixes ; la progression globale (« 3/12 ») reste au footer. Si 50 % des lignes visibles clignotent, la surface reste faible et la fréquence est de 1 Hz ; pas de réduction supplémentaire à prévoir. Le réglage `app.motion: static` reste la sortie (A-02).
2. **Ligne en cours et en échec à la fois** : priorité décidée ; l'échec réapparaît à la fin de l'opération, sa clé n'ayant pas changé. Footer avec suffixe (§1.2).
3. **Largeur des glyphes.** `●` `○` `◐` `◕` `◴` `◉` `◌` `⊗` `⊘` `⊖` sont, pour la plupart, de largeur « ambiguë » (la largeur de `◴` est à vérifier dans la rangée de test) (1 cellule en locale occidentale, 2 dans un terminal configuré en Est-asiatique) et certains Nerd Fonts les élargissent. `IconColumnWidth` = 2 couvre les deux cas, à condition que le `Cell` renvoie **le glyphe seul** et que `datatable` complète à 2 avec `runewidth`. Test à ajouter : la Rule 116 tient avec `runewidth.EastAsianWidth = true`. Un glyphe de 2 cellules colle alors au texte voisin : accepté, la colonne n'a pas de marge de plus.
4. **Terminal sans Nerd Font** (note seulement, hors périmètre, voir backlog §3.98). La pastille n'est pas affectée (glyphes Unicode standard), contrairement aux icônes de repos, qui s'afficheront comme des carrés. Mais certains polices de console (ex. Consolas sous Windows, hypothèse non vérifiée) n'ont pas `◴` `◕` `◌` `⊗` `⊘` `⊖` et les substituent par une police de repli, donc parfois plus larges. À consigner pour §3.98 ; l'utilisateur a confirmé le rendu dans son terminal (D7) ; les autres terminaux restent une note.
5. **`NO_COLOR` et terminaux 16 couleurs** : les quatre alias retombent sur des couleurs distinctes ou sur la couleur par défaut ; l'unicité des glyphes garantit la lecture. Aucun cas ne repose sur la teinte.
6. **Conteneur `exited` 0** : `⊖` neutre, tranché (D7). Un arrêt volontaire n'a rien à corriger ; rouge partout diluerait la couleur d'alerte (Rule 122 « color discipline ») et noierait les vrais `exited` non nuls et les `dead`.
7. **Rafraîchissement périodique** (métriques containers, ports en direct, lecture agents de 2 s) : ne déclenche aucun clignotement (donnée).
8. **Action `docker stop` instantanée** : la pastille `●`/`○` apparaît par l'état `busy` (priorité « en cours »), puis l'icône habituelle (conteneur `running`) ou le glyphe d'état observé revient au prochain sondage ; un échec reste au footer (non-objectif).
9. **Focus de formulaire.** `IconCircleSmall` (``, Nerd Font) signale le champ actif dans les formulaires. C'est une forme proche de `●` mais dans un autre écran, jamais dans une table : pas de collision, à rappeler dans l'aide.
10. **Ligne sans icône de repos** : cellule vide de largeur `IconColumnWidth`, jamais `◌`.

### Libellé de la légende de l'aide `?` (Rule 114, anglais US)

Une seule source dérivée de la table de glyphes (A-01 absorbe A-15). Base, présente dans chaque vue migrée :

```
Title: Activity indicator
Description: The first column shows what is happening on a row. The glyph carries the
meaning; the color repeats it. Nothing here relies on color alone.

  ●  ○   Running (blinks). Pauses to a steady ● when motion is off.
  ◴      Queued, waiting to start.
  ⊗      Failed. Stays until the next attempt on that row; the footer gives the cause.
  (icon) Idle: the row's usual icon, or an empty cell.

The footer describes the selected row's state in words.
Turn the blinking off with app.motion: static in the context file or in :cfg.
```

Libellés **validés** (D10), à une réserve : la fin de la dernière phrase (« or in :cfg ») suppose que `app.motion` est modifiable dans la vue de configuration. **À confirmer** (architect, comme `app.gauge_glyph`) ; sinon retirer « or in :cfg ».

Extension propre à `:jobs` : `◉ done · ⊘ cancelled · ⊖ skipped`.
Extension propre à `:agent-usage` : `◐ idle (no activity for 5 min) · ◉ done · ◌ unknown`.
Extension propre aux containers : `◕ restarting · ◐ paused · ◌ created · ⊖ exited (code 0) · ⊗ exited (non-zero code) or dead · ●/○ an action (stop, kill, remove) is running`. Pas de ligne `running` : un conteneur qui tourne montre son icône habituelle (D8).

35	| `⊗` | échec (opération échouée, conteneur `dead` ou `exited` non nul) | `ColorActivityFailed` | non, jamais |
36	| `◐` | suspendu : agent `idle`, conteneur `paused` | `ColorActivitySuspended` | non |
37	| `◕` | conteneur `restarting` | `ColorActivitySuspended` | non (fixe, tranché) |
38	| `◉` | terminé, **et rien d'autre** : job `done`, agent `done` | `ColorActivityNeutral` | non |
39	| `⊘` | annulé (job `cancelled`) | `ColorActivityNeutral` | non |
40	| `⊖` | sans action : job `skipped`, conteneur `exited` code 0 | `ColorActivityNeutral` | non |
41	| `◌` | inconnu / pas encore démarré : agent `unknown`, conteneur `created` | `ColorActivityNeutral` | non |
42	| repos | icône habituelle de la ligne (rôle `IconRole*` existant) ou cellule vide. **Un conteneur `running` est au repos** : état nominal (Rule 122), aucune pastille | rôle existant | non |
43	| mode « sans mouvement » | `●` fixe (la phase allumée) | `ColorActivityRunning` | non |

78	### 1.3 Choix tranchés (décision 7, 2026-11-06)
79	
80	Les options étudiées avant la décision sont abandonnées ; il ne reste que le choix et sa raison.
81	
82	- **Phase éteinte du clignotement : `○`, même couleur lavande.** Une capture figée se lit « quelque chose est là, en mouvement », jamais « rien » ; la couleur ne change pas (pas de scintillement de teinte) ; le contraste reste celui de l'état allumé (environ 7:1 sur la sélection). Écartés : `●` atténué en `ColorDim` (proche d'une cellule vide, échoue 3:1 : environ 2,5:1 sur le fond, 1,9:1 sous le curseur), `●` en `ColorText` (confondable avec un état terminé).
83	- **Conteneur `restarting` : `◕` orange fixe.** C'est un état observé, pas une opération lancée par DevDesk ; pas de dépendance au signal `WantsBlink` pour ce cas ; un `restarting` en boucle de crash change plus vite que le sondage docker, donc un clignotement synchronisé sur le tick serait trompeur ; `○` reste réservé à « en cours ».
84	- **« En file » : `◴` statique, `ColorActivityNeutral`.** Une file n'est pas une activité ; faire clignoter ce qui attend fait croire que ça avance, et un lot de 12 scans compterait 11 clignotants de plus sans information.
85	- **Conteneur `running` : aucune pastille** (D8). L'état nominal ne se colore pas (Rule 122, « color discipline ») ; la ligne garde son icône habituelle, et la pastille ne signale que ce qui s'écarte du nominal.

314	Précédence : error > warn > info > status. Un détail de ligne est de niveau `Status` (sans minuteur, recalculé à chaque trame), composé « détail de ligne · progression globale ». Le détail est tronqué d'abord (Rule 124 : la hauteur ne change pas).
315	
316	Ligne en cours (`ws`, ligne `api` sélectionnée, sync de 12 dépôts) :
317	
318	```
319	(blanc)
320	        ● Syncing ~/w/app/api · 3/12 repositories
321	```
322	
323	Niveau `Status`, texte de couleur ordinaire. Pas de spinner de footer ici : la pastille bouge déjà sur la ligne ; un spinner doublerait le mouvement.
324	
325	Ligne en erreur, en trois temps :
326	
327	| Temps | Niveau | Texte | Couleur |
328	|---|---|---|---|
329	| t = 0 à 3 s (l'échec arrive) | `Error`, avec minuteur | `Failed to scan ~/w/app/web — trivy could not pull the database` | `ColorFooterError`, gras |
330	| t > 3 s, ligne `web` sélectionnée | `Status`, persistant | `⊗ ~/w/app/web: last scan failed — trivy could not pull the database` | `ColorFooterInfo`, normal |
331	| t > 3 s, autre ligne sélectionnée | `Status` | le détail de cette ligne, ou la progression globale seule | idem |
332	
333	La pastille rouge fixe persiste jusqu'à la prochaine tentative sur la ligne ; seul le texte de footer passe de l'événement à l'état (décision de l'architect, Q4). Si une opération est en cours sur la même ligne, l'échec masqué est en suffixe (§1.2). Si un autre `Error` arrive pendant les 3 s, il prend le pas (précédence inchangée).
334	
335	## 4. Fréquence et « en file »
336	
337	**Tranché (D7) : 1 Hz (500 ms allumé, 500 ms éteint), phase déduite de l'horloge.**
338	
339	| | 1 Hz (recommandé) | 2 Hz |
340	|---|---|---|
341	| WCAG 2.3.1 (≤ 3 flashs/s) | 1 flash/s : marge de 3 | 2 flashs/s : sous le seuil, marge de 1,5 |
342	| Perception | pouls calme, ne distrait pas pendant la lecture d'un tableau | réveille l'œil, se lit comme une alerte |
343	| Coût (SSH) | une réécriture de cellule par ligne par seconde | le double |
344	| Cadence du tick routeur | 500 ms (déjà prévue par l'architect) | 250 ms |
345	| Détection de l'état gelé | un blocage de plus de 1 s se voit | idem, plus vite |
346	
347	Justification complémentaire : la surface qui clignote est minuscule (une cellule par ligne), la variation de luminance est modeste (anneau contre disque, même couleur), et rien ne clignote en rouge. Toutes les pastilles clignotent **en phase** : un décalage entre lignes créerait un effet de vague qui augmente le flash perçu. La phase vient du temps du message de tick (`on = (t.UnixMilli() / 500) % 2 == 0`) : survit à un changement de cadence, testable. 2 Hz resterait une constante à changer si le pilote la jugeait trop lente (le premier point de contrôle peut le rouvrir).
348	
349	**« En file » : statique** (`◴`, `ColorActivityNeutral`). Voir §1.3. Passage `◴` à `●`/`○` à la prise en charge ; le tick démarre alors, une seule fois.
350	
351	## 5. Cas limites
352	
353	1. **Plusieurs pastilles simultanées dans une vue.** Toutes en phase, pas de plafond. Un lot de N scans donne 1 en cours + (N−1) en file : un seul clignotant (le tick est partagé) et N−1 `◴` fixes ; la progression globale (« 3/12 ») reste au footer. Si 50 % des lignes visibles clignotent, la surface reste faible et la fréquence est de 1 Hz ; pas de réduction supplémentaire à prévoir. Le réglage `app.motion: static` reste la sortie (A-02).
354	2. **Ligne en cours et en échec à la fois** : priorité décidée ; l'échec réapparaît à la fin de l'opération, sa clé n'ayant pas changé. Footer avec suffixe (§1.2).
355	3. **Largeur des glyphes.** `●` `○` `◐` `◕` `◴` `◉` `◌` `⊗` `⊘` `⊖` sont, pour la plupart, de largeur « ambiguë » (la largeur de `◴` est à vérifier dans la rangée de test) (1 cellule en locale occidentale, 2 dans un terminal configuré en Est-asiatique) et certains Nerd Fonts les élargissent. `IconColumnWidth` = 2 couvre les deux cas, à condition que le `Cell` renvoie **le glyphe seul** et que `datatable` complète à 2 avec `runewidth`. Test à ajouter : la Rule 116 tient avec `runewidth.EastAsianWidth = true`. Un glyphe de 2 cellules colle alors au texte voisin : accepté, la colonne n'a pas de marge de plus.
356	4. **Terminal sans Nerd Font** (note seulement, hors périmètre, voir backlog §3.98). La pastille n'est pas affectée (glyphes Unicode standard), contrairement aux icônes de repos, qui s'afficheront comme des carrés. Mais certains polices de console (ex. Consolas sous Windows, hypothèse non vérifiée) n'ont pas `◴` `◕` `◌` `⊗` `⊘` `⊖` et les substituent par une police de repli, donc parfois plus larges. À consigner pour §3.98 ; l'utilisateur a confirmé le rendu dans son terminal (D7) ; les autres terminaux restent une note.
357	5. **`NO_COLOR` et terminaux 16 couleurs** : les quatre alias retombent sur des couleurs distinctes ou sur la couleur par défaut ; l'unicité des glyphes garantit la lecture. Aucun cas ne repose sur la teinte.
358	6. **Conteneur `exited` 0** : `⊖` neutre, tranché (D7). Un arrêt volontaire n'a rien à corriger ; rouge partout diluerait la couleur d'alerte (Rule 122 « color discipline ») et noierait les vrais `exited` non nuls et les `dead`.
359	7. **Rafraîchissement périodique** (métriques containers, ports en direct, lecture agents de 2 s) : ne déclenche aucun clignotement (donnée).
360	8. **Action `docker stop` instantanée** : la pastille `●`/`○` apparaît par l'état `busy` (priorité « en cours »), puis l'icône habituelle (conteneur `running`) ou le glyphe d'état observé revient au prochain sondage ; un échec reste au footer (non-objectif).
361	9. **Focus de formulaire.** `IconCircleSmall` (``, Nerd Font) signale le champ actif dans les formulaires. C'est une forme proche de `●` mais dans un autre écran, jamais dans une table : pas de collision, à rappeler dans l'aide.
362	10. **Ligne sans icône de repos** : cellule vide de largeur `IconColumnWidth`, jamais `◌`.
363	
364	### Libellé de la légende de l'aide `?` (Rule 114, anglais US)
365	
366	Une seule source dérivée de la table de glyphes (A-01 absorbe A-15). Base, présente dans chaque vue migrée :
367	
368	```
369	Title: Activity indicator
370	Description: The first column shows what is happening on a row. The glyph carries the
371	meaning; the color repeats it. Nothing here relies on color alone.
372	
373	  ●  ○   Running (blinks). Pauses to a steady ● when motion is off.
374	  ◴      Queued, waiting to start.
375	  ⊗      Failed. Stays until the next attempt on that row; the footer gives the cause.
376	  (icon) Idle: the row's usual icon, or an empty cell.
377	
378	The footer describes the selected row's state in words.
379	Turn the blinking off with app.motion: static in the context file or in :cfg.
380	```
381	
382	Libellés **validés** (D10), à une réserve : la fin de la dernière phrase (« or in :cfg ») suppose que `app.motion` est modifiable dans la vue de configuration. **À confirmer** (architect, comme `app.gauge_glyph`) ; sinon retirer « or in :cfg ».
383	
384	Extension propre à `:jobs` : `◉ done · ⊘ cancelled · ⊖ skipped`.
385	Extension propre à `:agent-usage` : `◐ idle (no activity for 5 min) · ◉ done · ◌ unknown`.
386	Extension propre aux containers : `◕ restarting · ◐ paused · ◌ created · ⊖ exited (code 0) · ⊗ exited (non-zero code) or dead · ●/○ an action (stop, kill, remove) is running`. Pas de ligne `running` : un conteneur qui tourne montre son icône habituelle (D8).
387	
388	## 5 bis. Écarts avec les user stories et les règles
389	
390	| Où | Écart | Proposition |
391	|---|---|---|
392	| A-01, critère 1 (`theme.IconStyle(rôle)` avec rôles `IconRole*` surchargeables) | Les couleurs d'état sont des alias fermés, pas des rôles `icon_*` (l'architect Q8 et `app-shell.md` disent déjà non). Les rôles `IconRole*` ne servent qu'à l'icône de **repos**. | Intégré : A-01, critère 1 (D4). |
393	| A-13, critère 2 (`unknown` en dim) | `ColorDim` échoue à 3:1, surtout sous la sélection. | Intégré : `unknown` en `ColorActivityNeutral`, glyphe `◌` (A-13, critère 2). |
394	| A-01, critère 2 / A-02, critère 2 | « glyphe statique différent du repos et de l'erreur » : satisfait par `●` fixe. | Intégré : `●` nommé dans A-02, critère 2. |
395	| **Rule 121** (`IconOK`, `IconError`, `IconWarning` pour tout statut de tableau) | Les pastilles `◉` `⊗` `◐` remplacent ces icônes dans la première colonne d'activité, ce qui contredit la lettre de la règle (`:jobs`, containers). | **Amendement accepté (D9)** : Rule 121 « ne s'applique pas à la colonne d'activité ; les autres colonnes d'état gardent `IconOK`/`IconError`/`IconWarning` ». Toute colonne Verdict ou Update reste inchangée. Écrit avec le composant (A-01, critère 10). |
396	| Rule 125 | La colonne est sans titre, `SizingFixed`, sans `Less`/`Search` : conforme. Elle devient aussi la colonne d'activité, et non plus seulement d'icône de type. | Paragraphe ajouté à la Rule 125 avec le composant (A-01, critère 10) ; renvoi au garde-fou dans A-17. |
397	| Rule 122, couleur discipline | Pas de vert pour terminé : conforme. Cinq glyphes en `ColorText` pour des états différents n'est pas de la « couleur partout » : c'est de la couleur neutre. Le clignotement lavande est le seul accent. | Aucun. |
398	| A-14, critère 2 (« `dead` rouge fixe », « `running` non vert ») | Remplacé par la décision 8 : un conteneur `running` n'a **aucune pastille** (icône habituelle) ; `◉` ne désigne plus qu'un état « terminé ». | Intégré : A-14, critères 2 et 3. |
399	| A-15 (légende) fusionnée dans A-01 par l'architect | La légende est dérivée de la table de glyphes, texte au §5. | Intégré : A-01, critère 9. |
400	| Aide containers existante (`view.go:220`) | Elle décrit `IconCaretRight`, `IconSmallPause`, etc. | À remplacer par la légende ci-dessus (A-14, critère 8). |
401	
402	## 6. Décisions de l'utilisateur et points restants
403	
404	### Tranchés (2026-11-06)
405	
406	| Ancienne question | Décision |
407	|---|---|
408	| Q1 Jeu de glyphes dans le terminal | Gardé tel quel (D7) : `●` et `◉` se distinguent, **pas de repli `✓`** ; l'ancien glyphe en quart (U+25D4) remplacé partout par `◴` |
409	| Q2 Phase éteinte | `○`, même couleur (D7) |
410	| Q3 Fréquence | 1 Hz (D7) |
411	| Q4 Conteneur `exited` code 0 | `⊖` neutre (D7) |
412	| Q5 `restarting` | `◕` orange fixe, ne clignote pas (D7) |
413	| Q6 « En file » | `◴` statique (D7) |
414	| Q7 Amendement de la Rule 121 | Accepté (D9) |
415	| Q8 `unknown` / `created` | Couleur neutre, pas dim (D7) |
416	| Q9 Libellés de la légende `?` et du footer | Validés (D10), sauf la réserve « or in :cfg » ci-dessous |
417	| Q10 Conteneur `running` en `◉` | **Remplacé** : aucune pastille, icône habituelle (D8) ; `◉` = terminé uniquement |
418	
419	### Restent à confirmer
420	
421	1. **« or in :cfg »** dans la légende : `app.motion` est-il modifiable dans la vue de configuration ? À vérifier par l'architect (`stories.md`, question ouverte 7).
422	2. **Test de contraste** : les rapports du §2.1 sont des calculs à la main ; le test de A-01 (critère 7) doit les confirmer, pour chaque alias, sur le fond et sur `ColorTableLineSelected` (`stories.md`, question ouverte 8).

content.content:
1	// Package datatable is the shared mechanism behind the application's tables.
2	//
3	// What was shared before was only the *look* — theme.DefaultTableStyles,
4	// TableStylesForState/ForSeverity, components.FilterBar, theme.TimeAgo. Column
5	// widths, sorting, sort arrows, filter matching, cursor clamping and
6	// cursor-to-object resolution were written out again in each of the fifteen
7	// tables, and drifted:
8	//
9	//   - Rule 116's width invariant is broken by five of the twelve copies, which
10	//     clamp per column after the remainder has been computed (see widths.go).
11	//   - Two of eight clamp the cursor when the row count shrinks; the rest leave
12	//     it dangling, and oci_resources compensates by jumping to the top on every
13	//     filter toggle, throwing away the scroll position.
14	//   - Nine getSelectedX() replay filter-then-sort by hand to map a cursor back
15	//     to an object, with nothing tying that ordering to the one the rows were
16	//     built from. If they drift, the action lands on the wrong object and says
17	//     nothing. That is the duplication worth removing on correctness grounds.
18	//
19	// Here the filtered, sorted slice is built once and kept, so Selected() cannot
20	// disagree with what is on screen, and Cell func(T) string gives styled text
21	// nowhere to go — Rule 122 by construction rather than by review.
22	package datatable
23	
24	import (
25		"slices"
26		"sort"
27		"strings"
28	
29		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/spinner"
30		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/table"
31		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
32		"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
33	
34		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
35		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
36	)
37	
38	// Sizing is what decides a column's width: the number it declared, or the
39	// content it holds. Every column states one — the zero value is refused by
40	// TestEveryColumnDeclaresItsSizing rather than given a meaning, because a
41	// default here would decide for twenty tables nobody had looked at (D12).
42	type Sizing int
43	
44	const (
45		// SizingUnset is the zero value, and means nothing. See the test above.
46		SizingUnset Sizing = iota
47		// SizingFixed takes exactly the width declared. For a count, a state, an
48		// icon — anything whose size was known when the code was written.
49		SizingFixed
50		// SizingContent takes the width of its widest visible value, never below
51		// MinWidth and never above MaxWidth. For paths, URLs, addresses, image
52		// references: values whose length is a property of the data.
53		SizingContent
54	)
55	
56	// Column describes one column and how to get its value out of an item.
57	type Column[T any] struct {
58		Title string
59		// Sizing is the column's nature (see above). It has no default.
60		Sizing Sizing
61		// MinWidth is the width a SizingFixed column takes, and the floor a
62		// SizingContent column is never squeezed under.
63		//
64		// It is a floor now, not the request it used to be: the shortfall comes out
65		// of the content columns down to their MinWidth, and after that whole
66		// columns are removed rather than emptied one cell at a time (widths.go).
67		// The name stays MinWidth on a fixed column, where it *is* the width, for
68		// the reason §3.45 gives: Width would be false on a content column that
69		// grows past it, where MinWidth is merely redundant on a fixed one — a
70		// redundant name is bearable, a false one is not.
71		MinWidth int
72		// MaxWidth caps a SizingContent column. 0 means no ceiling, and there is no
73		// global default: a ceiling chosen once would apply to columns nobody has
74		// looked at, and a full IPv6 address is 45 cells — so the first "reasonable"
75		// default re-truncates exactly what the measurement was for. Meaningless on
76		// SizingFixed, where MinWidth already is the width.
77		MaxWidth int
78		// Optional marks a column that may be dropped whole when the table does not
79		// fit, before any column that is not. Orthogonal to Sizing because all four
80		// combinations exist: the interface error counters have an exact width and
81		// are also the first thing worth losing.
82		Optional bool
83		// DescFirst makes the first `.` that lands on this column sort it
84		// descending, the second ascending. For count columns, where ascending is
85		// the useless end (see Config.SortDesc). Meaningless without Less.
86		DescFirst bool
87		// DropFirst moves an Optional column to the head of the queue: it goes
88		// before every other Optional one, wherever it sits on screen. Meaningless
89		// without Optional, which is the flag that decides whether a column may go
90		// at all.
91		//
92		// It exists because drop() reads the column order as an order of
93		// importance, and that is true of every column whose place is chosen by
94		// what it *is*. A gauge's place is chosen by what it *illustrates* — it has
95		// to sit beside the number it draws, in the middle of the table, or it
96		// stops being read as that number's picture (§3.71). Left to position
97		// alone, the containers table would shed its I/O counters to keep two bars
98		// that are the most expendable thing on the row.
99		//
100		// A bool rather than a rank: two tiers is what the case needs, and an int
101		// would invite every table to number its columns against each other.
102		DropFirst bool
103		// YieldsToContent lets this Optional column be removed before a required
104		// content column (SizingContent, not Optional) is cut below its widest
105		// value. It acts only while this column is the one drop() would remove
106		// next: set it on a prefix of the table's drop order, or it is never
107		// reached before the content is cut. The drop order itself does not
108		// change, only the moment. Optional content columns are still cut first.
109		// Meaningless without Optional. Off, the solver is unchanged.
110		YieldsToContent bool
111		// TruncateHead cuts the start of an over-long value rather than its end.
112		//
113		// A flag per column rather than a rule derived from Sizing, because the
114		// answer depends on the column and not on its nature: a URL, an image
115		// reference and a path share their prefix and are told apart by their end,
116		// while an address is identified by the network it starts with. It cannot
117		// be left to Cell either — Cell does not know the width it will be rendered
118		// at, and that is deliberate: it is what makes the value measurable.
119		TruncateHead bool
120		// Flex is the column's share of the space left over once every column has
121		// what it wants. 0 takes no part; the leftover is split between the
122		// flexible ones by weight.
123		//
124		// Flex says who receives the surplus, never who needs it — which is why it
125		// cannot decide widths on its own: the ports table gave Process 110 cells
126		// for "svchost.exe" at 200 columns while Peer Address stayed frozen at 26,
127		// cutting an IPv6 endpoint in half. That is what Sizing answers.
128		Flex int
129		// Cell returns the text for this column. Plain text only: it is measured
130		// and truncated before anything is applied to it, and runewidth counts an
131		// escape sequence's bytes as width — a styled string is cut mid-escape and
132		// bleeds over every row below it (Rule 122). Taking a string rather than a
133		// styled value is what makes that unexpressible here.
134		//
135		// It must be pure and cheap. The rendering calls it once per visible cell;
136		// the measurement calls it once per cell of every visible row, off screen
137		// included. Nothing can check that — it is an arbitrary closure — so it is
138		// stated here rather than tested.
139		Cell func(T) string
140		// Style colours the cell after it has been measured and truncated, which is
141		// the only order in which colour is safe (see render.go). Nil leaves the
142		// cell in the table's own colours.
143		//
144		// On a row a view has coloured whole via SelectedStyles (error, busy, a CVE
145		// severity), it is not consulted: that row is handed to styles.Selected
146		// whole, and a colour inside it would end the highlight mid-row. On the
147		// plain "normal" selection it *is* consulted — see render.go's cellStyle,
148		// which repaints the shared background on every cell instead of once on an
149		// outer wrap, so per-cell colour and the highlight no longer fight.
150		Style func(T) lipgloss.Style
151		// Cut and TailStyle split a cell into two coloured runs instead of Style's
152		// one: Style colours the first Cut(item) cells of the *finished* text —
153		// already measured, truncated and padded to the column's width — and
154		// TailStyle colours the rest. Both nil (the ordinary case, every column but
155		// the containers load gauges and the workspaces Git Status) leaves Style covering the whole cell as
156		// before.
157		//
158		// This is not the gradient Rule 122 forbids: nothing styled is ever
159		// measured. Cut reads a plain, already-final string — the split happens
160		// after truncation, at the same point Style already does its colouring —
161		// so it is the same "measure first, colour after" order applied twice
162		// instead of once, not an exception to it. It stays two runs rather than an
163		// arbitrary list: neither caller (the load gauges, the workspaces Git
164		// Status cell) has needed more than two, and Cut, a
165		// bare integer, is cheaper to reason about than a slice of spans that only
166		// ever holds two elements.
167		//
168		// Dropped only for a row a view has coloured whole — error, busy, a CVE
169		// severity — for the same reason Style is: a two-run cell still needs its
170		// own reset between the runs, which that solid background cannot afford.
171		// The plain "normal" selection consults both: each run repaints
172		// ColorTableLineSelected and bold itself, the same per-cell repaint that makes a
173		// single-run selected cell safe, so a load gauge keeps its fill/track
174		// split under the cursor instead of collapsing to Style's colour alone.
175		Cut       func(T) int
176		TailStyle func(T) lipgloss.Style
177		// Spans splits a cell into any number of coloured runs, left to right, over
178		// the *fitted* text (measured, truncated and padded first). Widths below 0
179		// count as 0, a zero-width span renders nothing, spans past the cell's width
180		// are clipped and the cells left after the last span take Style. A nil or
181		// empty result takes the one-run path. Spans takes precedence over
182		// Cut/TailStyle; a column declaring both is rejected by a source test.
183		// Like Cut, widths count runes, so the cell must hold single-width glyphs.
184		// Dropped, like Cut/TailStyle, on a row a view has coloured whole.
185		Spans func(T) []Span
186		// Less sorts by this column. Nil means the column cannot be sorted by, and
187		// `.` skips it.
188		Less func(a, b T) bool
189		// Search is what the text filter matches against. Nil means the column does
190		// not participate.
191		Search func(T) string
192	}
193	
194	// Config is everything a view has to say about its table.
195	type Config[T any] struct {
196		Columns []Column[T]
197		// Tokens are the toggle filters shown in the bar (Rule 136).
198		Tokens []components.FilterToken
199		// TokenMatch decides whether an item passes the active toggles. Nil means
200		// the toggles are ignored, which is only sensible with no Tokens.
201		TokenMatch func(item T, active map[string]bool) bool
202		// SortColumn is the column sorted by on open; -1 for no initial sort.
203		SortColumn int
204		// SortDesc opens the table on the descending order of SortColumn. It exists
205		// for the count columns, where ascending is the useless end: an inventory
206		// sorted by CRITICAL wants the worst target first, and cycling `.` past
207		// ascending to reach it on every open is not a default.
208		SortDesc bool
209		// Key identifies an item across rebuilds, and is what the busy set is held
210		// on. Nil switches the busy facility off entirely, which is the default:
211		// most tables have no action to run on a row.
212		//
213		// It cannot be a `Busy func(T) bool` on this struct instead. Columns are

296	// New builds a table from its configuration.
297	func New[T any](cfg Config[T]) Model[T] {
298		cols := make([]table.Column, len(cfg.Columns))
299		for i, c := range cfg.Columns {
300			cols[i] = table.Column{Title: c.Title, Width: c.MinWidth}
301		}
302		t := table.New(table.WithColumns(cols), table.WithFocused(true), table.WithHeight(10))
303	
304		bar := components.NewFilterBar()
305		if len(cfg.Tokens) > 0 {
306			bar = components.NewFilterBarWithTokens(cfg.Tokens)
307		}
308	
309		m := Model[T]{cfg: cfg, table: t, bar: bar, sortColumn: cfg.SortColumn, sortDesc: cfg.SortDesc}
310		// A frame from the start: a table whose view never calls AdvanceSpinner —
311		// one rendered in the same frame the action began — would otherwise show an
312		// empty status cell, which reads as "nothing is happening".
313		m.AdvanceSpinner()
314		// Through setStyles rather than the table alone: a table rendered before
315		// anything calls applyStyles — one built and drawn in the same frame — would
316		// otherwise render with the zero Styles, which carries no cell padding and
317		// so lays out two cells narrower per column than every width was solved for.
318		m.setStyles(theme.DefaultTableStyles())
319		// The invariant the rest of the file rests on: sortColumn is either -1 or a
320		// column that can actually be sorted by. Settling it once here is what lets
321		// CycleSort and sorted() stop re-checking — and what stops `.` getting stuck
322		// flipping the direction of a column with no comparator.
323		if m.sortColumn >= len(cfg.Columns) || (m.sortColumn >= 0 && cfg.Columns[m.sortColumn].Less == nil) {
324			m.sortColumn = -1
325			// A direction with no column to apply it to would put the header arrow
326			// on nothing and make `.` open on descending.
327			m.sortDesc = false
328		}
329		return m
330	}

701	// rebuild filters, sorts, writes the rows and puts the cursor somewhere real.
702	func (m *Model[T]) rebuild() {
703		m.visible = m.sorted(m.filtered())
704	
705		// The natural widths are taken here because the cells are already being
706		// built: the measurement is a lipgloss.Width per cell on a walk that
707		// happens anyway. Promoting them to the solver is a separate decision
708		// (see Remeasure) — this only keeps the answer current.
709		//
710		// The header counts. A content column narrower than its own title truncates
711		// the one cell that says what the column is, and "the width the content
712		// wants" plainly includes being able to name itself.
713		m.natural = make([]int, len(m.cfg.Columns))
714		for j, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
715			m.natural[j] = lipgloss.Width(c.Title)
716		}
717	
718		rows := make([]table.Row, len(m.visible))
719		for i, item := range m.visible {
720			cells := make(table.Row, len(m.cfg.Columns))
721			for j, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
722				cells[j] = c.Cell(item)
723				if w := lipgloss.Width(cells[j]); w > m.natural[j] {
724					m.natural[j] = w
725				}
726			}
727			rows[i] = cells
728		}
729		m.table.SetRows(rows)
730	
731		// bubbles/table leaves the cursor where it was, so a list that just got
732		// shorter strands it past the end until the user presses a key. It also
733		// reports -1 while there are no rows at all, and that has to be taken back
734		// when rows return — a filter typed past its last match and then corrected
735		// would otherwise leave the table showing rows none of which is selected.
736		switch cursor := m.table.Cursor(); {
737		case len(rows) == 0:
738			// -1 is bubbles' own "nothing selected", and what it reports for a
739			// table that never had rows. Leaving the old index would make an empty
740			// list the one state where the cursor points past the end.
741			m.table.SetCursor(-1)
742		case cursor >= len(rows):
743			m.table.SetCursor(len(rows) - 1)
744		case cursor < 0:

746		}

13	// Why this package renders its own rows rather than calling table.Model.View().
14	//
15	// bubbles/table builds a cell as:
16	//
17	//	m.styles.Cell.Render(style.Render(runewidth.Truncate(value, width, "…")))

19	// — it measures the value *before* styling it, with runewidth, which counts an
20	// escape sequence's bytes as width. A seven-cell string carrying a colour
21	// measures 28, so it is truncated in a column twice wide enough, and the cut
22	// lands inside the escape: "\x1b[38;2;166;2…". The unterminated sequence then
23	// bleeds over every row below. That is Rule 122, and no configuration of
24	// bubbles avoids it — bubbles v1.0.0 has the same line.
25	//
26	// Here the order is inverted: Cell returns plain text, which is what gets
27	// measured and truncated, and Style is applied to the finished cell. Nothing
28	// styled is ever measured, so the failure is unexpressible rather than
29	// forbidden by review.
30	//
31	// The other half of the reason is the selected row. bubbles hands the whole
32	// joined row to styles.Selected, and a colour inside it closes with a reset
33	// that takes the selection background with it for the rest of the line — the
34	// highlight ends mid-row. A row a view has coloured whole (error, busy, a CVE
35	// severity) still drops per-cell colours for exactly that reason (see
36	// cellStyle). The plain "normal" selection instead gives every cell the
37	// *same* background itself, which sidesteps the defect rather than reproduces
38	// it — a reset between two cells never uncovers anything but that shared
39	// background again.

44	// View renders the header and the window of rows around the cursor.
45	func (m *Model[T]) View() string {
46		cols := m.table.Columns()
47		// At least one line under the header. A terminal too short to hold a single
48		// row leaves Height() at 0, and a table that renders literally nothing
49		// closes the viewport border onto itself — bubbles' viewport always emitted
50		// that line, and two views check for it at 20x1.
51		rows := max(m.table.Height(), 1)
52	
53		lines := make([]string, 0, rows+1)
54		lines = append(lines, m.headerLine(cols))
55	
56		cursor := m.table.Cursor()
57		for i := m.offset; i < len(m.visible) && len(lines) <= rows; i++ {
58			lines = append(lines, m.rowLine(cols, m.visible[i], i == cursor))
59		}
60		// Pad to the full height so the viewport border does not close in on a
61		// short list. bubbles' viewport did this with unstyled lines; filling them
62		// with the app background is Rule 115 applied to the one part of the table
63		// that had escaped it.
64		blank := theme.EmptyLineBg(contentWidth(cols))
65		for len(lines) <= rows {

148	// bytes as width, so text has to be measured while it is still plain.

210	//     on Cell, so a column that declares no Style rendered in whatever
211	//     foreground the terminal happens to use — the theme had no say. Four views
212	//     had written `Foreground(theme.ColorText)` into a Style of their own to get
213	//     it back, which is the shape a missing default takes.
214	//
215	// The busy row, for its part, does not consult `Style` either: what it says
216	// is that an operation is in progress, and a color by severity or by state
217	// on top of that would say the opposite. The spinner's glyph keeps
218	// `ColorHighlight`, the rest goes to `DimStyle` — the displayed state is in
219	// the process of ceasing to be true.
220	func (m *Model[T]) cellStyle(c Column[T], item T, selected, busy bool, at int) lipgloss.Style {
221		if selected {
222			if !m.preserveColumnColors {
223				// Neither background nor text here: they would hide those of styles.Selected.
224				return m.styles.Cell
225			}
226			style := m.styles.Cell
227			if c.Style != nil {
228				style = c.Style(item).Padding(0, 1)
229			}
230			if _, unset := style.GetForeground().(lipgloss.NoColor); unset {
231				style = style.Foreground(theme.ColorText)
232			}
233			return style.Background(theme.ColorTableLineSelected).Bold(true)
234		}
235		if busy {
236			style := theme.DimStyle
237			if at == m.cfg.StatusColumn {
238				style = lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(theme.ColorHighlight)
239			}
240			return style.Padding(0, 1).Background(theme.ColorBackground)
241		}
242		if c.Style == nil {
243			return m.styles.Cell.Foreground(theme.ColorText).Background(theme.ColorBackground)
244		}
245		style := c.Style(item).Padding(0, 1)
246		if _, unset := style.GetForeground().(lipgloss.NoColor); unset {
247			style = style.Foreground(theme.ColorText)
248		}
249		if _, unset := style.GetBackground().(lipgloss.NoColor); unset {
250			style = style.Background(theme.ColorBackground)
251		}
252		return style
253	}

261	// multiRunCell renders a cell that colours more than one stretch of its text:
262	// Column.Spans when it answers a non-empty list, else Cut/TailStyle. ok is false
263	// for an ordinary one-run cell, which the caller renders through cellStyle.
264	func (m *Model[T]) multiRunCell(c Column[T], item T, fitted string, selected bool) (string, bool) {
265		if c.Spans != nil {
266			if spans := c.Spans(item); len(spans) > 0 {
267				return m.renderRuns(m.spanRuns(c, item, spans, fitted, selected)), true
268			}
269			return "", false
270		}
271		if c.TailStyle == nil {
272			return "", false
273		}
274		return m.splitCellRun(c, item, fitted, selected), true
275	}

277	// spanRuns lays spans over the fitted text from left to right: a negative width
278	// counts as 0, a zero-width span yields no run, what overflows the cell is cut
279	// and the cells left after the last span take c.Style. Widths are in runes, so
280	// like Cut they assume single-width glyphs.
281	func (m *Model[T]) spanRuns(c Column[T], item T, spans []Span, fitted string, selected bool) []run {
282		runes := []rune(fitted)
283		var runs []run
284		pos := 0
285		for _, s := range spans {
286			end := min(pos+max(s.Width, 0), len(runes))
287			if end > pos {
288				runs = append(runs, run{string(runes[pos:end]), m.runStyle(s.Style, selected)})
289				pos = end
290			}
291		}
292		if pos < len(runes) {
293			runs = append(runs, run{string(runes[pos:]), m.runStyle(m.styleOf(c.Style, item), selected)})
294		}
295		return runs
296	}

298	// splitCellRun renders a two-colour cell: c.Style covers the first c.Cut(item)
299	// cells of the already-fitted text, c.TailStyle the rest, as two runs.
300	//
301	// fitted is exactly cols[i].Width runes (fit() guarantees it), so slicing by
302	// rune index is safe: every glyph a caller uses here — braille, ASCII, the
303	// truncation marker — is single-width, which callers are expected to keep
304	// true rather than this function verifying it.
305	//
306	// selected mirrors cellStyle's own selected branch: on the plain "normal"
307	// selection (m.preserveColumnColors), both runs repaint ColorTableLineSelected and
308	// bold themselves instead of each keeping their unselected background — the
309	// same per-cell repaint that makes a single-run selected cell safe applies
310	// unchanged to two runs, since a reset between them only ever uncovers that
311	// same shared background, immediately repainted by the run that follows.
312	// This is what lets a load gauge (Cut/TailStyle) keep its fill/track split
313	// under the cursor instead of collapsing to Style's fill colour alone.
314	func (m *Model[T]) splitCellRun(c Column[T], item T, fitted string, selected bool) string {
315		runes := []rune(fitted)
316		cut := min(max(c.Cut(item), 0), len(runes))
317		return m.renderRuns([]run{
318			{string(runes[:cut]), m.runStyle(m.styleOf(c.Style, item), selected)},
319			{string(runes[cut:]), m.runStyle(m.styleOf(c.TailStyle, item), selected)},
320		})
321	}

323	// renderRuns renders the runs of one cell side by side. The column's 1-cell
324	// padding goes on the outer edge of the first and last run as literal spaces
325	// rather than lipgloss's Padding property, so runs don't each add their own pair
326	// and open a gap at a boundary. Every run given is rendered, empty or not:
327	// callers that must not emit an empty styled run drop it beforehand.
328	func (m *Model[T]) renderRuns(runs []run) string {
329		var b strings.Builder
330		for i, r := range runs {
331			text := r.text
332			if i == 0 {
333				text = " " + text
334			}
335			if i == len(runs)-1 {
336				text += " "
337			}
338			b.WriteString(r.style.Render(text))
339		}
340		return b.String()
341	}

375	// clampOffset moves the scroll window the least it can to keep the cursor in
376	// it. bubbles kept this in an unexported viewport; owning the rendering means
377	// owning the offset too.

380	// the cursor on screen keeps the scroll position — the property SetItems was
381	// written to protect.

383		height := max(m.table.Height(), 1)
384		last := max(len(m.visible)-height, 0)
385	
386		m.offset = min(max(m.offset, 0), last)
387	
388		switch cursor := m.table.Cursor(); {
389		case cursor < 0: // nothing selected: an empty table scrolls nowhere
390			m.offset = 0
391		case cursor < m.offset:
392			m.offset = cursor
393		case cursor >= m.offset+height:
394			m.offset = cursor - height + 1
395		}
396	}

701	// rebuild filters, sorts, writes the rows and puts the cursor somewhere real.
702	func (m *Model[T]) rebuild() {
703		m.visible = m.sorted(m.filtered())
704	
705		// The natural widths are taken here because the cells are already being
706		// built: the measurement is a lipgloss.Width per cell on a walk that
707		// happens anyway. Promoting them to the solver is a separate decision
708		// (see Remeasure) — this only keeps the answer current.
709		//
710		// The header counts. A content column narrower than its own title truncates
711		// the one cell that says what the column is, and "the width the content
712		// wants" plainly includes being able to name itself.
713		m.natural = make([]int, len(m.cfg.Columns))
714		for j, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
715			m.natural[j] = lipgloss.Width(c.Title)
716		}
717	
718		rows := make([]table.Row, len(m.visible))
719		for i, item := range m.visible {
720			cells := make(table.Row, len(m.cfg.Columns))
721			for j, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
722				cells[j] = c.Cell(item)
723				if w := lipgloss.Width(cells[j]); w > m.natural[j] {
724					m.natural[j] = w
725				}
726			}
727			rows[i] = cells
728		}
729		m.table.SetRows(rows)
730	
731		// bubbles/table leaves the cursor where it was, so a list that just got
732		// shorter strands it past the end until the user presses a key. It also
733		// reports -1 while there are no rows at all, and that has to be taken back
734		// when rows return — a filter typed past its last match and then corrected
735		// would otherwise leave the table showing rows none of which is selected.
736		switch cursor := m.table.Cursor(); {
737		case len(rows) == 0:
738			// -1 is bubbles' own "nothing selected", and what it reports for a
739			// table that never had rows. Leaving the old index would make an empty
740			// list the one state where the cursor points past the end.
741			m.table.SetCursor(-1)
742		case cursor >= len(rows):
743			m.table.SetCursor(len(rows) - 1)
744		case cursor < 0:
745			m.table.SetCursor(0)
746		}
747		m.afterCursorMove()
748	}

13	// Why this package renders its own rows rather than calling table.Model.View().
14	//
15	// bubbles/table builds a cell as:
16	//
17	//	m.styles.Cell.Render(style.Render(runewidth.Truncate(value, width, "…")))
18	//
19	// — it measures the value *before* styling it, with runewidth, which counts an
20	// escape sequence's bytes as width. A seven-cell string carrying a colour
21	// measures 28, so it is truncated in a column twice wide enough, and the cut
22	// lands inside the escape: "\x1b[38;2;166;2…". The unterminated sequence then
23	// bleeds over every row below. That is Rule 122, and no configuration of
24	// bubbles avoids it — bubbles v1.0.0 has the same line.
25	//
26	// Here the order is inverted: Cell returns plain text, which is what gets
27	// measured and truncated, and Style is applied to the finished cell. Nothing
28	// styled is ever measured, so the failure is unexpressible rather than
29	// forbidden by review.
30	//
31	// The other half of the reason is the selected row. bubbles hands the whole
32	// joined row to styles.Selected, and a colour inside it closes with a reset
33	// that takes the selection background with it for the rest of the line — the
34	// highlight ends mid-row. A row a view has coloured whole (error, busy, a CVE
35	// severity) still drops per-cell colours for exactly that reason (see
36	// cellStyle). The plain "normal" selection instead gives every cell the
37	// *same* background itself, which sidesteps the defect rather than reproduces
38	// it — a reset between two cells never uncovers anything but that shared
39	// background again.

44	// View renders the header and the window of rows around the cursor.
45	func (m *Model[T]) View() string {
46		cols := m.table.Columns()
47		// At least one line under the header. A terminal too short to hold a single
48		// row leaves Height() at 0, and a table that renders literally nothing
49		// closes the viewport border onto itself — bubbles' viewport always emitted
50		// that line, and two views check for it at 20x1.
51		rows := max(m.table.Height(), 1)
52	
53		lines := make([]string, 0, rows+1)
54		lines = append(lines, m.headerLine(cols))
55	
56		cursor := m.table.Cursor()
57		for i := m.offset; i < len(m.visible) && len(lines) <= rows; i++ {
58			lines = append(lines, m.rowLine(cols, m.visible[i], i == cursor))
59		}
60		// Pad to the full height so the viewport border does not close in on a
61		// short list. bubbles' viewport did this with unstyled lines; filling them
62		// with the app background is Rule 115 applied to the one part of the table
63		// that had escaped it.
64		blank := theme.EmptyLineBg(contentWidth(cols))
65		for len(lines) <= rows {
66			lines = append(lines, blank)
67		}
68		return strings.Join(lines, "\n")
69	}

75	// Summing the declared columns' widths and adding two per column is the
76	// tempting version, and it is what every one of those tests did. It is wrong as
77	// soon as a column is dropped for want of room: the dropped column renders
78	// nothing and its padding goes back into the budget, so the formula asks for
79	// less than the line spans and fails on a layout that is correct. That
80	// disagreement was D61 seen from the other side.

84	// bubbles adds around each. It equals the viewport width less its two borders
85	// whenever Rule 116 holds, but it is measured rather than assumed so that a
86	// table that has never been resized still pads to its own content.
87	func contentWidth(cols []table.Column) int {
88		width := 0
89		for _, col := range cols {
90			if col.Width > 0 {
91				width += col.Width + cellPadding
92			}
93		}

116	// signal that disappears under the cursor is one the user loses exactly when
117	// they are looking at it.

119		_, busy := m.busyLabel(item)

123			if i >= len(cols) || cols[i].Width <= 0 {

155	}

157	// truncateHead keeps the *end* of the text, for the columns that declare it
158	// (Column.TruncateHead).
159	//
160	// A column of URLs, image references or paths shares its prefix on every row,
161	// so cutting the tail renders three identical cells that identify nothing —
162	// and it does so precisely when the column is squeezed to its floor, which is
163	// when it is hardest to read. Keeping the end is what tells the rows apart.
164	//
165	// runewidth rather than runes throughout: a cell is measured in terminal cells,
166	// and a CJK name counts two per rune.
167	func truncateHead(text string, width int) string {
168		total := runewidth.StringWidth(text)
169		if total <= width || width <= 0 {
170			return text
171		}
172		marker := runewidth.StringWidth(truncationMarker)
173		if width <= marker {
174			// No room for the marker and anything after it. Saying "there is more"
175			// with no idea what beats a single arbitrary character.
176			return runewidth.Truncate(truncationMarker, width, "")
177		}
178		return runewidth.TruncateLeft(text, total-(width-marker), truncationMarker)
179	}
180	
181	// cellStyle is the style one cell is rendered with.
182	//
183	// A row a view has coloured whole — error, busy, a CVE severity, via
184	// SelectedStyles or the busy override — drops every column's own colour and
185	// is handed to styles.Selected instead: a colour inside it would close with a
186	// reset that takes that solid background with it for the rest of the line.
187	// The highlight there answers "what state is this row in", and no per-cell
188	// colour is worth losing it to.
189	//
190	// **The plain "normal" selection is the opposite case** (§3.72 in the
191	// backlog, m.preserveColumnColors): each cell keeps its own colour and
192	// additionally repaints ColorTableLineSelected and bold **itself**, rather than
193	// once on an outer wrap. That is what makes it safe rather than a return of
194	// the defect above — every cell's own reset only ever uncovers the *same*
195	// background the next cell immediately repaints, so nothing but that
196	// background is ever exposed between two cells. styles.Selected still wraps
197	// the joined line afterward (rowLine), painting the same background again;
198	// by then it is redundant colour, not load-bearing, and it is what still
199	// pads the row out to the full content width.
200	//
201	// Off the selected row every cell carries an explicit foreground **and**
202	// background, whether or not the column asked for either. Both halves are
203	// forced for the same reason and each fixes its own defect:
204	//
205	//   - Background: lipgloss does not inherit one (Rule 115), and the app's
206	//     viewport style only reaches the cells that emit nothing of their own. One
207	//     coloured cell would otherwise end its line with a reset and strip the
208	//     background from everything to its right.
209	//   - Foreground: neither theme.DefaultTableStyles() nor bubbles' own sets one
210	//     on Cell, so a column that declares no Style rendered in whatever
211	//     foreground the terminal happens to use — the theme had no say. Four views
212	//     had written `Foreground(theme.ColorText)` into a Style of their own to get
213	//     it back, which is the shape a missing default takes.
214	//
215	// The busy row, for its part, does not consult `Style` either: what it says
216	// is that an operation is in progress, and a color by severity or by state
217	// on top of that would say the opposite. The spinner's glyph keeps
218	// `ColorHighlight`, the rest goes to `DimStyle` — the displayed state is in
219	// the process of ceasing to be true.
220	func (m *Model[T]) cellStyle(c Column[T], item T, selected, busy bool, at int) lipgloss.Style {
221		if selected {
222			if !m.preserveColumnColors {
223				// Neither background nor text here: they would hide those of styles.Selected.
224				return m.styles.Cell
225			}
226			style := m.styles.Cell
227			if c.Style != nil {
228				style = c.Style(item).Padding(0, 1)
229			}
230			if _, unset := style.GetForeground().(lipgloss.NoColor); unset {
231				style = style.Foreground(theme.ColorText)
232			}
233			return style.Background(theme.ColorTableLineSelected).Bold(true)
234		}
235		if busy {
236			style := theme.DimStyle
237			if at == m.cfg.StatusColumn {
238				style = lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(theme.ColorHighlight)
239			}
240			return style.Padding(0, 1).Background(theme.ColorBackground)
241		}
242		if c.Style == nil {
243			return m.styles.Cell.Foreground(theme.ColorText).Background(theme.ColorBackground)
244		}
245		style := c.Style(item).Padding(0, 1)
246		if _, unset := style.GetForeground().(lipgloss.NoColor); unset {
247			style = style.Foreground(theme.ColorText)
248		}
249		if _, unset := style.GetBackground().(lipgloss.NoColor); unset {
250			style = style.Background(theme.ColorBackground)
251		}
252		return style
253	}
254	
255	// run is one coloured stretch of an already-fitted cell.
256	type run struct {
257		text  string
258		style lipgloss.Style
259	}
260	
261	// multiRunCell renders a cell that colours more than one stretch of its text:
262	// Column.Spans when it answers a non-empty list, else Cut/TailStyle. ok is false
263	// for an ordinary one-run cell, which the caller renders through cellStyle.
264	func (m *Model[T]) multiRunCell(c Column[T], item T, fitted string, selected bool) (string, bool) {
265		if c.Spans != nil {
266			if spans := c.Spans(item); len(spans) > 0 {
267				return m.renderRuns(m.spanRuns(c, item, spans, fitted, selected)), true
268			}
269			return "", false
270		}
271		if c.TailStyle == nil {
272			return "", false
273		}
274		return m.splitCellRun(c, item, fitted, selected), true
275	}
276	
277	// spanRuns lays spans over the fitted text from left to right: a negative width
278	// counts as 0, a zero-width span yields no run, what overflows the cell is cut
279	// and the cells left after the last span take c.Style. Widths are in runes, so
280	// like Cut they assume single-width glyphs.
281	func (m *Model[T]) spanRuns(c Column[T], item T, spans []Span, fitted string, selected bool) []run {
282		runes := []rune(fitted)
283		var runs []run
284		pos := 0
285		for _, s := range spans {
286			end := min(pos+max(s.Width, 0), len(runes))
287			if end > pos {
288				runs = append(runs, run{string(runes[pos:end]), m.runStyle(s.Style, selected)})
289				pos = end
290			}
291		}
292		if pos < len(runes) {
293			runs = append(runs, run{string(runes[pos:]), m.runStyle(m.styleOf(c.Style, item), selected)})
294		}
295		return runs
296	}
297	
298	// splitCellRun renders a two-colour cell: c.Style covers the first c.Cut(item)
299	// cells of the already-fitted text, c.TailStyle the rest, as two runs.
300	//
301	// fitted is exactly cols[i].Width runes (fit() guarantees it), so slicing by
302	// rune index is safe: every glyph a caller uses here — braille, ASCII, the
303	// truncation marker — is single-width, which callers are expected to keep
304	// true rather than this function verifying it.
305	//
306	// selected mirrors cellStyle's own selected branch: on the plain "normal"
307	// selection (m.preserveColumnColors), both runs repaint ColorTableLineSelected and
308	// bold themselves instead of each keeping their unselected background — the
309	// same per-cell repaint that makes a single-run selected cell safe applies
310	// unchanged to two runs, since a reset between them only ever uncovers that
311	// same shared background, immediately repainted by the run that follows.
312	// This is what lets a load gauge (Cut/TailStyle) keep its fill/track split
313	// under the cursor instead of collapsing to Style's fill colour alone.
314	func (m *Model[T]) splitCellRun(c Column[T], item T, fitted string, selected bool) string {
315		runes := []rune(fitted)
316		cut := min(max(c.Cut(item), 0), len(runes))
317		return m.renderRuns([]run{
318			{string(runes[:cut]), m.runStyle(m.styleOf(c.Style, item), selected)},
319			{string(runes[cut:]), m.runStyle(m.styleOf(c.TailStyle, item), selected)},
320		})
321	}
322	
323	// renderRuns renders the runs of one cell side by side. The column's 1-cell
324	// padding goes on the outer edge of the first and last run as literal spaces
325	// rather than lipgloss's Padding property, so runs don't each add their own pair
326	// and open a gap at a boundary. Every run given is rendered, empty or not:
327	// callers that must not emit an empty styled run drop it beforehand.
328	func (m *Model[T]) renderRuns(runs []run) string {
329		var b strings.Builder
330		for i, r := range runs {
331			text := r.text
332			if i == 0 {
333				text = " " + text
334			}
335			if i == len(runs)-1 {
336				text += " "
337			}
338			b.WriteString(r.style.Render(text))
339		}
340		return b.String()
341	}
342	
343	// styleOf evaluates an optional per-item style function; nil gives the zero style.
344	func (m *Model[T]) styleOf(fn func(T) lipgloss.Style, item T) lipgloss.Style {
345		if fn == nil {
346			return lipgloss.NewStyle()
347		}
348		return fn(item)
349	}
350	
351	// runStyle applies the same foreground/background defaulting cellStyle gives
352	// a single-run cell, minus the Padding — renderRuns already pads with
353	// literal characters — so a multi-run cell is indistinguishable from a one-run
354	// one everywhere but the run boundaries.
355	//
356	// selected forces the shared selection background and bold weight
357	// unconditionally, exactly as cellStyle's selected branch does for a
358	// single-run cell — unlike the unselected path below, this overrides
359	// whatever background the run's own style already set (GaugeTrackStyle
360	// sets one explicitly), because the selected row's background is the
361	// highlight itself, not a fallback for an unset one.
362	func (m *Model[T]) runStyle(style lipgloss.Style, selected bool) lipgloss.Style {
363		if _, unset := style.GetForeground().(lipgloss.NoColor); unset {
364			style = style.Foreground(theme.ColorText)
365		}
366		if selected {
367			return style.Background(theme.ColorTableLineSelected).Bold(true)
368		}
369		if _, unset := style.GetBackground().(lipgloss.NoColor); unset {
370			style = style.Background(theme.ColorBackground)
371		}
372		return style
373	}
374	
375	// clampOffset moves the scroll window the least it can to keep the cursor in
376	// it. bubbles kept this in an unexported viewport; owning the rendering means
377	// owning the offset too.
378	//
379	// The window is only moved when the cursor has left it, so a reload that keeps
380	// the cursor on screen keeps the scroll position — the property SetItems was
381	// written to protect.
382	func (m *Model[T]) clampOffset() {
383		height := max(m.table.Height(), 1)
384		last := max(len(m.visible)-height, 0)
385	
386		m.offset = min(max(m.offset, 0), last)
387	
388		switch cursor := m.table.Cursor(); {
389		case cursor < 0: // nothing selected: an empty table scrolls nowhere
390			m.offset = 0
391		case cursor < m.offset:
392			m.offset = cursor
393		case cursor >= m.offset+height:
394			m.offset = cursor - height + 1
395		}
396	}
397	
398	// Offset reports the first visible row, for tests that check the window
399	// follows the cursor without going through the rendered string.
400	func (m *Model[T]) Offset() int { return m.offset }
401

355	
356	A column with no opinion should return the zero `lipgloss.Style` rather than
357	naming the theme's text colour itself.
358	
359	### A row an action is running on (§3.22)
360	
361	A row says two things: what the object **is**, and what is **happening** to it.
362	They share one glyph on purpose — one column answers "what about this row" — and
363	`datatable` owns the one rule that follows: **busy wins over state**, because
364	`exited` is precisely what the action is about to change.
365	
366	```go
367	datatable.Config[T]{
368	    Key:          func(c docker.Container) string { return c.ID }, // nil ⇒ facility off
369	    StatusColumn: 0,                                               // the cell the spinner replaces
370	}
371	
372	m.table.MarkBusy(id, "Stopping web")  // from Update, never a Cmd (Rule 110)
373	m.table.ClearBusy(id)                 // on *every* outcome, failures included
374	m.table.IsBusy(id)                    // the guard
375	m.table.BusyLabels()                  // sorted, for the footer
376	m.table.AdvanceSpinner()              // from the view's own spinner tick
377	```
378	
379	**It cannot be a `Busy func(T) bool` on the config.** Columns are built once in
380	`New` and close over nothing — that is why `imageRow` exists — so a predicate
381	there would have to close over the view's map of in-flight actions. Separating
382	the identity (`Key`) from the state is what avoids it, and it buys the thing
383	that matters most: **`IsBusy` answers for an object whose row does not exist
384	yet**, so it is also the guard on a confirm path. It is also what survives the
385	periodic refresh, which replaces the items mid-action.
386	
387	The spinner's **frame lives in the table, its tick stays in the view**: a
388	spinner needs a `Cmd`, and this package returns none.
389	
390	Rendering, and each part is a decision:
391	
392	- The status cell shows the spinner **on the selected row too** — a signal that
393	  vanishes under the cursor is lost exactly when it is being looked at.
394	- Off the cursor the row goes `DimStyle`, the spinner `ColorHighlight`, and the
395	  column's own `Style` is dropped.
396	- **On** the cursor the highlight itself changes
397	  (`theme.TableStylesForState("busy")`), overriding whatever `SelectedStyles`
398	  returned — a colour inside the joined row would close with a reset and end the
399	  highlight mid-row (`render.go`).
400	- The override is applied **when the row is drawn**, not when it is built, so
401	  the stored cells do not go stale as the frame advances. Tests assert on
402	  `View()`, not on `Table().Rows()`.
403	
404	The status column must **not be sortable**: `askFor` reserves `width(Title)+2`
405	for a column carrying a `Less`, which is expensive for a glyph.
406	
407	**Which cell the spinner spends is a decision per table**, and it is the same
408	decision every time: the one the user does not need while the action runs. Only
409	`containers` gained a column, because only it has a state worth a column of its
410	own; everywhere else the spinner rides an existing cell, which is §3.16's
411	argument about the clone checkbox — a column costs cells on every screen to say
412	nothing on all but one row.
413	
414	| Table | Key | Cell the spinner takes | Actions |
415	|---|---|---|---|
416	| `containers` | container ID | a status column of its own (the state icon left the Image cell) | stop, restart, pause/resume, remove |
417	| `oci` images | image ID | `ID` — it neither sorts nor searches | remove |
418	| `oci` networks | network ID | `ID` | remove |
419	| `oci` volumes | name | `Driver` — a volume has no ID, so its **name** is the one cell that cannot go | remove |
420	| `oci` registries | URL | `Logged` — precisely what the operation is about to change | login, logout |
421	| `netdiag` ports | **PID** | `State` | kill |
422	
423	Two of those keys are worth the note. The ports table keys on the **PID, not the
424	socket**, so every row of a process spins at once — which is what happens, the
425	kill takes them all. The registries table keys on the **URL**, which is the one
426	place D40's rule does not apply, and it does not apply because the *operation*
427	is host-scoped: one `docker login` really does change the answer for every entry
428	on that host.
429	
430	`oci_resources` gathers `BusyLabels()` from **all four tabs**, not the active
431	one: an action started on Images goes on running after `tab`, and a spinner that
432	stopped turning because the user looked elsewhere would read as a hang on the
433	way back. The spinner tick has to keep being scheduled while anything is busy —
434	that is what `advanceBusySpinners()` reports.
435	
436	Deliberately outside this:
437	
438	- **Scans** — their spinner is in the Scanned column and they do not block the
439	  object the same way.
440	- **`prune`** — it acts on no row, so marking every row would say something
441	  false. It gets a footer line rendered from the view's own state (`m.pruning`),
442	  like `syncStatusLine` (§3.17), because a footer *message* expires after three
443	  seconds (Rule 128) and `docker stop` outlives that by seven.
444	- **`workspaces`** — it already had all of this, its own way (`scanningPaths`,
445	  `syncingPaths`, `deletingPaths`, `busy(path)`), and is in fact where the
446	  design came from. Its delete was the one action its own machinery did not
447	  know about, and §3.23 step 1 taught it rather than migrating the view.
448	  Migrating would be a refactor of working code across the one busy notion that
449	  is *not* one object, one action: scan and sync exclude each other across
450	  nested paths, a sync targets a tree rather than a row, and the spinner does
451	  not spend the same cell for every operation.
452	
453	**Every table in the application is a `datatable`** (§3.21 moved the last four:
454	Registries, the registry browser's tags, network-inspect and netdiag's results).
455	A new table uses it; there is no second way to build one, and `bubbles/table` is
456	imported outside this package only for its `Styles` type.
457	
458	The Registries tab is the one worth knowing about, because it shows **two
459	populations in one table** — the configured entries, and one group's discovered
460	members after `→`. `datatable.Model[T]` is generic over a single `T`, so
461	`registryRow` carries both and holds the index of the config entry it stands
462	for, `-1` for a member. That index is what `getSelectedRegistry` resolves
463	through: indexing `m.registries` by row number is right only while the table
464	neither sorts nor filters, which is exactly the dependency nothing signalled.
465	`explorerRow` exists for the same reason.
466	
467	Three views keep a filter of their own, and deliberately. `security` selects
468	findings **by tab**, and `status` drives both its tables from one search box so
469	the header counts agree — in both cases the view filters and calls `SetItems`,
470	because a `FilterBar` query narrows a list that is already settled and these
471	decide which rows exist at all. `security` also calls `GotoTop` explicitly on a
472	tab change, which is the reset `SetItems` does not make. Its **severity** goes
473	the other way: four cumulative tokens the table owns, and its sort and its
474	search are the table's too. The
475	registry browser is the third: its text filter and its registry filter narrow
476	the tags *before* the table sees them, and its bar is drawn in the OCI view's
477	own footer rather than the table's. Its **sort** is the table's — `.` cycles
478	Tag and Updated through `CycleSort`, and `SetSort` is what puts a new search
479	back on the default order.
480	
481	`status` is the two-table case: two `datatable.Model` plus a focus helper.
482	`Focus` and `Blur` carry the styles with them (Rule 118), so a tab switch does
483	not touch `SetStyles`.

460	members after `→`. `datatable.Model[T]` is generic over a single `T`, so
461	`registryRow` carries both and holds the index of the config entry it stands
462	for, `-1` for a member. That index is what `getSelectedRegistry` resolves
463	through: indexing `m.registries` by row number is right only while the table
464	neither sorts nor filters, which is exactly the dependency nothing signalled.
465	`explorerRow` exists for the same reason.
466	
467	Three views keep a filter of their own, and deliberately. `security` selects
468	findings **by tab**, and `status` drives both its tables from one search box so
469	the header counts agree — in both cases the view filters and calls `SetItems`,
470	because a `FilterBar` query narrows a list that is already settled and these
471	decide which rows exist at all. `security` also calls `GotoTop` explicitly on a
472	tab change, which is the reset `SetItems` does not make. Its **severity** goes
473	the other way: four cumulative tokens the table owns, and its sort and its
474	search are the table's too. The
475	registry browser is the third: its text filter and its registry filter narrow
476	the tags *before* the table sees them, and its bar is drawn in the OCI view's
477	own footer rather than the table's. Its **sort** is the table's — `.` cycles
478	Tag and Updated through `CycleSort`, and `SetSort` is what puts a new search
479	back on the default order.
480	
481	`status` is the two-table case: two `datatable.Model` plus a focus helper.
482	`Focus` and `Blur` carry the styles with them (Rule 118), so a tab switch does
483	not touch `SetStyles`.

# DEVDESK-98 — Break down a session's tokens by category, model and agent (S-10)

Story S-10 (`docs/product/agent-usage-monitor/stories.md`), Plane DEVDESK-98, epic E2.
Delivered in two PRs: **PR 1, the bar** (steps 1–4), **PR 2, the panel** (steps 5–9).
Steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 are independent and can run in parallel.

## Acceptance criteria (summary)

1. Agents level: one column per agent, a fixed-width stacked bar, 4 segments in the
   order Input, Output, Cache write, Cache read, proportional to tokens
   (sum of `ByModel` = `Agent.Tokens`).
2. Segments sum to the exact width (largest remainder); a segment under half a cell
   may hold 0 cells (the `theme.GaugeFillWidth` doctrine); an agent with no token
   shows a dim `-`.
3. ~~Without colour the four categories stay distinguishable: four different glyphs.~~
   **Replaced — deviation accepted by the user (2026-11-05):** the four segments use
   **one glyph** (the containers gauge's, `app.gauge_glyph`) and are told apart by
   **colour alone**. New criterion: four distinct colours, with enough contrast on
   every shipped theme, never a severity or gauge colour (dedicated tests, step 2).
   Without colour the bar only says "this agent has tokens"; the exact split stays
   readable without colour in the In / Out / Cache read / Cache write columns and in
   the Breakdown tab. *The Plane story and `stories.md` must be amended (pm).*
4. "Breakdown" panel: three blocks in percentages — by category (Input, Output,
   Cache write 5 min, Cache write 1 h, Cache read), by model (`ByModel` merged,
   the unnamed bucket = `unknown`), by agent (role + short ID). Each block sums to
   100.0 % (residue absorbed like the Share column); token totals = the header's
   `Tokens` field.
5. Session with no token: dim `-` cells, no division by zero.
6. Active session: bar and panel recomputed with each read (DEVDESK-45 chain); the
   panel describes the whole session and ignores the `/` filter (like Billed).
7. Rules 130 (greyed when nothing to show), 114 (help), 108 and 116 at every
   width; counters only (no prompt or tool content).

Out of scope: dollars, bar in the sessions list, prices, time curve, export.
